messages.subject: Re: [GSoC R] R granted 31 slots for GSoC 2019 !
messages.subject_clean: [GSoC R] R granted 31 slots for GSoC 2019 !
messages.body_plain:
Excellent news for the R and open source communities!!
We already have the selected students at:

https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/organizations/4934391420157952/#projects

This would not be possible without all your work, thanks Toby and Brian!

El miércoles, 24 de abril de 2019, 17:45:55 (UTC-3), Brian G. Peterson escribió:
> R has been granted 31 slots for this year's Google Summer of Code.
>
> This is more slots than we have had in prior years, and shows a lot of
> trust on Google's part (most organizations get one or two slots total).
>
> We now need to be good stewards of that trust and responsibility.
>
> Students:
> Hold on, you'll know whether your proposal has been selected in two
> weeks.  Please don't ask the mentors for your project idea if you';ve
> been accepted, we cannot tell you.  Google reserves the right of
> communication to selected or rejected students to itself.
>
> Mentors:
> Toby and I will begin the process of preliminary slot allocations to
> projects.  *Nothing is Final Yet*.  We still need final de-duplication
> from Google, we need to validate that we have enough mentors for
> projects, and several other administrative steps.
>
> The most important thing for mentors to remember: you *may not*
> communicate with students about acceptance or rejection until *after*
> the Google announcements on May 6th.
>
> Next most important, Toby and I may need more information from you.
> Especially if you had multiple applications, or have asked us for
> multiple slots, we have more work to do.  We need to make sure that
> there are enough mentors to cover multiple slots, and that you have a
> plan for managing multiple projects (it is a lot of work).  If we ask
> you for something, please get back to us as quickly as you can.
> Google's deadlines are firm, and we don't have any wiggle room on
> those.  Our slot allocation is final (from our side) on May 1.
>
> If something doesn't look right on your Dashboard, or your project
> applications, please contact Toby and me via private email as soon as
> possible.
>
> As always, if you have any questions, please reach out.
>
> Regards,
>
> Brian
>
> --
> Brian G. Peterson
> http://braverock.com/brian/
> Ph: 773-459-4973
> IM: bgpbraverock
>

messages.subject: [R-GSoC] Happy coding! ... and a few administrative details
messages.subject_clean: [R-GSoC] Happy coding! ... and a few administrative details
messages.body_plain:
Congratulations again to our 31 GSoC students for 2019!

The coding period has officially started (yesterday).

By now students should have their development environments set up, and
you should be in frequent communication with your mentors. You and your
mentors should know which source code repository(ies) you will be
committing code into, and you should be planning to commit code
(almost) every day.  Google guidelines expect you to be doing this full
time during the summer, so please work more to front-load any time you
will be spending on other commitments, and communicate with your
mentors about any changes.

We understand that the schedule and priorities will change.  The key
here is communication with your mentors, and continuous, visible
progress towards goals.

If any mentors are not associated with the correct project slots, I
need to know *now*.  I believe that I can only assign mentors through
the end of May.  So I ask all mentors and students to please check your
projects on the summerofcode website.

As always, if you have any questions or issues, please email Toby and
me.

Happy Coding,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock
